findings.location: Model > How does it work?; LLM Justification [^r2]
findings.finding: The correction substantially repairs the process description: it gives tick order, dilemma-driven Signal/Inquire choice, targets, updates, and choice thresholds. However, it states aspiration is initialized Uniform[0,1] without recording a publisher-text conflict. Appendix A “Stochasticity” (JASSS lines 417–421) says aspiration is a floating-point value from 0 to <3, while “Initialisation/Create agents” (lines 441–442) says uniformly distributed [0,1]. The note silently selects the latter. In addition, the final habit rule is summarized via threshold comparisons, without explicitly retaining the text’s statement that a novel preference replaces the previous habit only if significantly more satisfying and less dissonant; the footnote cites general overview/Sections 2.1–2.4 rather than Appendix A subsections for these implementation details.
findings.fix: Flag both aspiration ranges as an internal source conflict instead of selecting Uniform[0,1]. Explicitly state the novel-choice replacement condition or clarify how the described sequential threshold comparison implements it. Update [^r2] to cite Appendix A “Stochasticity,” “Initialisation,” “Signal or inquire,” “Signal,” “Inquire,” “Set dissonances,” and “Choose alternative” (JASSS lines 417–461, 479–535).
